In the medial compartment,  
  Bony marrow SI and condral cartilage at medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau are preserved. 
  Medial meniscus; preserved. 
  Medial collateral ligament: Preserved. 
  Medial gastrocnemius: Preserved.  
  Semimenbranosus tendon: Unremarkable.   
  Semitendinosus tendon: preserved. 
  Pes anserine tendon: preserved.  
  Baker cyst: not seen. 
  
 Lateral compartment 
  Preservation of cartilage at weightbaring lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau.  
  Radial tear at anterior root of lateral meniscus, suspicious oblique vertical tear at anterior to body of lateral meniscus with illdefine hyperSI in T2WI along mid body of lateral meniscus; combine contusional injury is suggested.

  Lateral meniscus; increase fluid SI and thickness at anterior root of lateral meniscus; contusional injury is suggested. 
  Lateral collateral ligament: Thickening at proximal femoral attach site, increase SI in T2W with peritendinous fluid; Grade 1 sprain is suggested. 
  Popliteus tendon: Visualized fluid surrounding and thinning of tendon suspicious of partial tear. 
  Poplitiofibular ligament ; is unidentified. 
  Meniscofemoral ligament: preserved. 
  Biceps femoris: Unremarkable. 
  Iliotibial band: Intact. 
  Lateral gastrocnemius: intact. 
  Tibiofibular joint; unremarkable. 
  
 Patellofemoral joint 
  Preserve marrow SI within patella and femur with minimal joint effusion. 
  No definite chondrosis at medial and lateral facet articular cartilage.  
  Quadriceps tendon; intact 
  Patella tendon; intacte infact and within normal alignment.  
  Medial and latera patellofemoral retinaculum; preserved. 
  Thin superior patella plica. 
  Minimal joint effusion. 
  
 Intercondylar notch 
  PCL: Preserved. 
  ACL: Preserved. 
 The other surrounding musculature and neurovascular structure is unremarkable.  Radial tear at anterior root of lateral meniscus, suspicious oblique vertical tear at anterior to body of lateral meniscus with illdefine hyperSI in T2WI along mid body of lateral meniscus; combine contusional injury is suggested. 
  Minimal joint effusion at knee.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right knee injury 2 years prior. Instability and locking. Limited range of motion.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus which appears diminutive and irregular, extending into the body. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis without tear. The iliotibial band is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. No patellofemoral subluxation. The TT-TG distance measures 4 mm, within normal limits.

Mild quadriceps insertional tendinosis without tear. The patellar tendon is intact.

Preserved patellofemoral articular cartilage. Focal full thickness cartilage denuding posterior nonweightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. The remainder of the lateral femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved. There is subtle thinning of articular cartilage involving the peripheral posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. The remainder of the medial femorotibial articular cartilage is preserved.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Popliteus tendinosis without tear. Quadriceps tendinosis without tear.
3. Focal areas of medial and lateral femorotibial chondrosis as detailed above.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda. Meniscopatía.
Hallazgos:
No no hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio
proximal del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de los componentes del
complejo medial sin alteraciones.
Imagen lineal horizontal del cuerno anterior del menisco lateral que podría otra rotura. Esto se asocia a
fibrilación marginal del cuerpo y cuerno anterior.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que no impresiona contactar con
la superficie articular, sin caracteres que sugieran una rotura actual.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial del aspecto posterior de platillo tibial lateral. El resto de los cartílagos
femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de
distribución difusa de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo con signos de rotura con líquido perifascial hacia caudal.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del tendón
rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Probable esguince de bajo grado del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial.
Probable rotura del cuerno anterior del menisco lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 del aspecto posterior de platillo tibial lateral.
Condropatía rotuliana con lesiones grado dos y tres.
Leve derrame articular. Quiste poplíteo con probable rotura.
Tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal. Signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la
rótula

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: pain effusion; bilateral knee pain for one month, no known injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Multifocal areas of subchondral edema along the lateral tibial plateau and femoral condyles.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small, ruptured Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Periligamentous edema about the lateral collateral ligament with intact fibers.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.  

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Edema of the popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis as well as subchondral marrow edema along both tibial plateau and femoral condyles and edema of the posterolateral corner. Findings are concerning for early inflammatory arthritis, for which aspiration should be considered.
